source_facts: No t(n) or clock interval is assigned.
answer: The assigned position rule does not determine a propagation speed or c. A speed follows only conditionally after an independently proposed time map is supplied.

derived_from_source.claim: The index is a dimensionless integer. For an index increment of one, x(n+1)-x(n)=L.
L per index increment has units of length, not length/time. No elapsed time is provided for the denominator.

assumptions: t(n)=n tau, with tau>0 a fixed time interval measured in a stated time unit.
Positions and clock readings describe the same proposed sequence of events.
proposed_clock.conditional_derivation: For n>=0, delta x=L and delta t=tau. The signed discrete interval velocity is v=L/tau; its speed is |L|/tau. When L is taken as a positive length scale in the increasing-x convention, this speed is L/tau.
proposed_clock.continuous_limit: A continuous instantaneous velocity requires an extra interpolation or continuous motion model. The discrete quotient alone establishes only interval velocity.

nonidentifiability_counterexample.assumptions: Take any proposed tau>0. Both t1(n)=n tau and t2(n)=2n tau are permitted by the unchanged position-only source.
nonidentifiability_counterexample.derivation: They give respectively v1=L/tau and v2=L/(2tau). For L!=0 these differ while every assigned x(n) is identical. Thus the position source cannot select a unique speed.
nonidentifiability_counterexample.degenerate_case: If L=0 all sampled positions coincide; the position-only source still supplies no physical clock or independently identified propagation constant.

limits: The conditional quotient requires a nonzero elapsed time; tau=0 makes it undefined.

For fixed |L|>0, taking proposed tau toward zero from above makes |L|/tau unbounded, and taking tau without bound makes it approach zero. These are mathematical parameter limits, not evidence of physically achievable speeds.
Unequal proposed clock intervals would give step-dependent L/[t(n+1)-t(n)]; constant interval speed requires the additional fixed-clock hypothesis.
The packet contains no calibration, measurement, dynamics or identification of c.

identification_with_c.definition_route: One may explicitly define a model parameter c:=|L|/tau. That definition labels the conditional ratio and does not derive or measure a pre-existing physical constant.
identification_with_c.evidence_route: If c denotes a specified physical propagation speed, its meaning, the event interpretation, independently calibrated length/time scales, and evidence that this process propagates at that speed must be supplied. Choosing tau=|L|/c from an already assumed c is circular as a derivation of c.
identification_with_c.scope: No validated physics result and no Aether-Flow result are claimed.

criterion_coverage.evidence: source_facts, derived_from_source and proposed_clock distinguish the three evidence states.
Dimensional argument and the two-clock counterexample show the missing time denominator and nonidentifiability.
Proposed t(n)=n tau gives conditional L/tau with explicit units, tau>0 and discrete/parameter limits.
identification_with_c states a definition route, required physical evidence and the circularity limit.
